question: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his mother with a history of multiple falls for the last 8 months. He was born at term without any perinatal complications. At birth, his weight and height were 57th and 62nd percentile for his age, respectively. For the first year, he had normal developmental milestones. He started walking at the age of 17 months and started climbing stairs at 2 years of age. For the last 8–10 months, he has been walking clumsily, has fallen multiple times, and is having difficulty standing from the sitting position. He is not able to climb the stairs now. Past medical history is unremarkable. His vaccinations are up-to-date. His maternal uncle had a similar history, and he became bed-bound at 12 years of age. During the physical examination, the patient stood up from sitting position slowly by placing hands on his knees. What additional findings will be present in this patient?

options.opb: Inability to release grasp after handshake
options.ope: Rash over shoulders and anterior chest

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Difficulty standing from sitting position" -> "Walking clumsily" -> "Frequent falls" -> "Difficulty climbing stairs" -> "Possible muscle weakness" -> "Progressive muscle weakness" -> "Difficulty with fine motor skills" -> "Possible genetic muscle disorder" -> "Family history of similar symptoms" -> "Likely genetic inheritance" -> "Muscular dystrophy presentation" -> "Possible Duchenne muscular dystrophy" -> "Additional findings may include pseudohypertrophy of the calf muscles" -> "Possible pseudohypertrophy of the calf muscles in Duchenne muscular dystrophy" -> "Likely presence of pseudohypertrophy of the calf muscles in this patient" -> "Pseudohypertrophy of the calf muscles" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation of difficulty standing from sitting position, walking clumsily, frequent falls, and difficulty climbing stairs is concerning for a possible genetic muscle disorder, likely Duchenne muscular dystrophy given the family history. Additional findings may include pseudohypertrophy of the calf muscles, which is a characteristic feature of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
analysis: The patient's presentation, along with the family history of a similar condition in the maternal uncle, strongly suggests Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The additional finding of pseudohypertrophy of the calf muscles is a characteristic feature of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This finding, in conjunction with the clinical history, supports the diagnosis of Duchenne muscular dystrophy in this patient.
